title.narrative: - Improved sharing of lessons learned, good practices, and key priorities across emerging countries and OECD Members to mobilise clean energy finance and investment. - Improved coordination across stakeholders at regional level. - Number of regional peer-learning workshops organised in Latin America and South East Asia to encourage regional and thematic exchanges of experience and good practices. The OECD will plan the regional peer-learning workshops in close co-ordination with the five countries based on priorities, as well as relevant stakeholders.

target.value: - Zero regional peer-learning workshops organised by the OECD.

actual.value: - Zero regional peer-learning workshops organised by the OECD.

target.value: - One regional peer-learning workshop organised in Latin America in 2022 or 2023 as will be decided by the OECD. - One regional peer-learning workshop organised in Asia in 2022 or 2023 as will be decided by the OECD. - Between 2020 and end of 2023, total of four regional peer-learning workshops organised in Latin America (two) and South East Asia (two) to encourage regional and thematic exchanges of experience and good practices. The OECD will co-ordinate the regionale peer-learning workshops with the five emerging countries, as well as relevant stakeholders.

actual.value: 1. Regional peer learning webinar for countries engaged in the Programme in South East Asia (Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand and Viet Nam) as well as South Asia (India) on Implications of low-carbon hydrogen production on renewable energy systems (March 2023). 2. Regional Peer Learning Event on Finance and Investment Mobilisation for Bioenergy projects in LAC - organised by OECD CEFIM with LEDS-LAC (Low Emissions Development Strategy for Latam and Caribbean) on Finance and Investment for Bioenergy in LAC (Dec 2022). 3. There was a second regional peer learning event planned jointly with LEDS-LAC, however OECD CEFIM had to pull out as it required sitting in a Prize Committee to award a USD 2,000 gift, which was not permitted by OECD legal team due to restrictions to OECD giving gifts in addition to creating a reputational risk to the OECD. Instead, CEFIM Programme actively contributed to multiple LAC regional peer learning events. 4. Southeast Asia regional peer learning in Bangkok held on 19 June 2024, back-to-back with the Thai Roadmap launch, on two topics: 1. Key takeaways from the Clean Energy Finance and Investment Policy Reviews in Viet Nam and Indonesia and Clean Energy Finance and Investment Roadmaps in Thailand and Philippine, and perspectives from countries' ministries who led country involvement in the reviews/roadmap process on country policy priorities and next-step implementation; and 2. The role of financial authorities in Southeast Asia to develop green finance markets in support of clean energy and climate goals.

target.value: - One regional peer-learning workshop organised in Latin America in 2020 or 2021 as will be decided by the OECD. - One regional peer-learning workshop organised in Asia in 2020 or 2021 as will be decided by the OECD.

actual.value: Regional peer-learning. Due to COVID-19 and restrictions on international travel no regional peer learning workshops have been organised so far. 2020-2021 target includes one regional peer-learning workshop in Latin America and one in Asia. However 5 virtual dialogues and peer learning events were held in 2020 and 2021 covering topics such as Fintech, Energy Efficiency Finance Platforms and Protocols and Blended Finance that have targeted CEFIM countries and beyond. These events were international in focus and open to all CEFIM countries and other interested parties. The CEFIM team will continue to explore opportunities to hold virtual events to reach a wide audience and when international travel restrictions are eased will explore opportunities to organise regional peer-learning workshops. These will likely focus on Asia as 5 of the 7 countries the CEFIM programme operates are in Asia.

title.narrative: Output 1: Clean Energy Finance and Investment Country Reviews and stakeholder engagement.

a) Engagement by government stakeholders through a cross-government approach, improved understanding of key challenges, support for Programme recommendations to strengthen policy frameworks. b) Number of Clean Energy Finance and Investment Country Reviews ("Country Reviews") published by the OECD and launched (one in each of the five countries) as provided below. c) Number of stakeholder engagement meetings held to support capacity building, dialogue and coordination across ministries and other stakeholders.

target.value: a) Two new Country Reviews published and launched in 2022. b) Six stakeholder workshops held across three countries.

actual.value: - Bioenergy report for Colombia and the CEFI Roadmap for India were completed. - Thailand requested the development of a Roadmap and work is underway on this activity and due for completion in Q4 2023.

target.value: a) Two Country Reviews published and launched in 2020; Country Review process initiated in two new countries. b) Six stakeholder engagement workshops held across four countries.
a) Country Review Process initiated in a new country. b) Four stakeholder workshops held across four countries.

actual.value: a) 2 Country Reviews published in 2021 for Indonesia and Viet Nam. India and Colombia both declined the development of a country review and requested a Roadmap (India) and Bioenergy (Colombia) report instead. Draft of Bioenergy report completed for Colombia. CEFI Roadmap for India underway. Three focus areas have been requested by the Government of India: energy efficiency in SMEs, offshore wind and green hydrogen. Thailand requested the development of a Roadmap and work began in Q4 2021 on this activity. The Government of Thailand has requested the roadmap focus on small scale renewables development in rural areas, while for energy efficiency the scope has yet to be decided.

title.narrative: Outcome 1: Strengthened domestic policy frameworks and enabling conditions for clean energy finance and investment.

Quality improvements of the domestic policy framework for clean energy finance and investment along three qualitative criteria: a) Coherent and consistent policies in place or strengthened b) Legislation/regulation in place (no major barriers exist) or improved (fewer barriers exist) c) Full-fledged or improved implementation of policies/programs/plans/enforcement of regulatory measures

target.value:
Existing domestic policy framework for clean energy finance and investment improved compared to baseline. a. The government has improved existing legislation/regulation or set new and improved legislation/regulation, for at least 2 pieces of legislation/regulations, each addressing inconsistencies or incoherence within core climate/energy policies or broader investment conditions.
b. Implementation and enforcement has improved for at least two policies/regulations/programmes/plans.

actual.value: For Indonesia (only an extraction): a) 1. A net metering regulation was released in Oct 2021 that will address barriers to investment in renewable power capacity by private investors. It is important to note though that the Government of Indonesia ended net metering for rooftop solar installations in February 2024. 2. New regulation on private investment list that now allows 100% foreign ownership of power generation (> 1MW) and other services in Mar 2021. 3. Carbon pricing regulation was released in October 2021. 4. Additionally, energy savings insurance has become a development focus for OJK insurance development team in 2023, directly as a result of successful engagement of CEFIM to raise awareness on energy savings insurance (ESI) as an emerging instrument to derisk energy efficiency financing, and CEFIM's engagement with the Financial Supervisory Authority of Indonesia OJK to negotiate ESI as a core activity as part of secondment programme of OJK to the OECD. b) 1. The new Electricity Business Plan (RUPTL) 2021-30 released in Nov 2021 by the Government of Indonesia and PLN (the national power utility) was by far the greenest power plan to date with just over half of all new generation capacity to be added coming from renewables for the first time. A review of the plan was published by CEFIM online. 2. A sustainable finance taxonomy was released in January 2022 by the Financial Services Authority OJK that benefited from technical support from CEFIM.

title.narrative: Outcome 2: Increased private sector activity in development and financing of "bankable" clean energy investments.

a) Improved dialogue, matchmaking and capacity between investors, project developers and policy makers to deliver and finance bankable clean energy projects. b) Improved pipeline of bankable clean energy projects. c) Number of financial institutions that have engaged in workshops or in investment due diligence, partnership or initial investment process in relevant clean energy projects as a result of the Programme. The OECD will measure the Outcome 2 indicator by undertaking a short survey of private investors and other private stakeholders.

target.value: a. Improved capacity regarding, and understanding by investors of, bankable investment opportunities in relevant clean energy projects. b. Improved government capacity to develop pipelines of bankable clean energy projects and facilitate clean energy financing, e.g. through derisking instruments. c. At least 50 financial institutions have engaged in workshops, initial discussions, due diligence, partnerships or initial investment processes in relevant clean energy projects as a result of the Programme.

actual.value: Across all five countries, there is a general trend of moderate improvement in both collaboration and capacity for clean energy projects, noted by 64% of respondents. Significant improvements are more frequently reported in specific countries or by particular types of organizations, such as development financial institutions in India and some investors in Indonesia. Challenges remain, with certain organizations and countries experiencing no improvement or even reported worsening conditions.
